A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CrossEarth-Gate and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Content can be reliably matched across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original cross-domain segmentation experiments, backbone and component ablations, and module-activation analyses in Tables 1-5 and the appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains the original experiments and adds module-combination, random-selection, gradient-saliency, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The spatial, semantic, and frequency toolbox and category-normalized Fisher-guided Top-k selection remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 documents the existing procedure rather than introducing a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 CASID climate transfers, two Potsdam-to-RescueNet transfers, and four Potsdam/Vaihingen and LoveDA adaptation scenarios. The new appendix analyses reuse existing coverage; 18 scenarios were already reported in v1.

E2.justification: Mona is removed from Tables 1-3 and the appendix qualitative comparisons. New Table 6 introduces a random-selection comparator, while the other named benchmark comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New supplementary evaluations introduce static module-combination and random-selection controls, plus training-time, memory, FLOPs, and throughput measurements. Existing splits, resolutions, batch sizes, and training budgets remain unchanged; newly disclosed optimizer settings do not establish changed experiments.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends the existing ablations with module-combination and random-selection tests (Table 6), Sub-versus-Tem activation comparisons (Figure 4), input-gradient saliency (Figure 5), and computational-overhead analysis (Table 7). These address additional questions about Fisher selection, module complementarity, specialization, and practical efficiency.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The selection-event counts and Fisher accumulation samples describe training operations, not experimental replication.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial diagnostic and resource results: Table 6 reports random selection at 58.7% Sub-source average alongside the retained Fisher result of 60.6%, and Table 7 reports 437 minutes of training and 2.12 images/second for the proposed method. Mona results are removed, and CrossEarth's parameter count changes from 304.2M to 3.0M in Tables 1-2. Retained benchmark mIoU scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The optimization objective, module equations, and KL/Fisher mathematical reasoning in Equations 1-10 are unchanged. The added pseudocode introduces no new mathematical definition, assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The toolbox and Fisher-selection contributions and the main efficiency/generalization claims remain the same. V3's abstract specifies '16 out of 18' benchmarks, clarifying coverage already stated in v1's introduction rather than changing the claim's scope.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of domain-specific activation patterns, module-specific saliency, and why Fisher selection produces stronger synergy than random gating. It also discusses measured selection overhead and deployment costs. Existing storage limitations, architectural/task boundaries, and exceptional failure cases remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds Algorithm 1, AdamW weight decay 0.05 and betas 0.9/0.999, augmentation references, and clarification of active-parameter ranges and the 3,000-step CASID selection interval. Module sizes and selection counts were already documented. Mona's implementation description and the promised code release are removed.

R1.justification: Seven references are added, including weather-model PEFT, Tianquan-S2S, A2-MAE, and Convolution Meets LoRA, mostly within existing citation lists. The broader positioning around specialized PEFT limitations and Fisher-guided adaptation is retained.

P1.justification: Changes include localized copyediting, updated affiliations, acknowledgments, and additional appendix subsections. Most exposition and the main section order remain intact; the existing qualitative discussion moves from C.3 to C.5.

P2.justification: The appendix display content expands with saliency Figure 5, analysis Tables 6-7, Algorithm 1, and an expanded/reordered Figure 4. Existing comparison tables and qualitative grids remove Mona entries. Figure 4's overall caption incorrectly retains descriptions that no longer match its panel ordering.

improvement.justification: The random-selection control and measured computational costs strengthen v1's evidence for Fisher gating and practical efficiency, while pseudocode and optimizer details aid reproduction. These provide a limited net gain: the new quantitative checks focus on one source domain, Mona comparisons disappear, hardware and uncertainty reporting remain absent, and some new presentation inconsistencies persist.
